title: Proxy and Chain of Responsibility
idea: Proxy stands in for an object with the same interface and controls access to it. Chain of Responsibility passes a request along handlers until one deals with it.
points: A proxy can check permissions, cache results or create the real object lazily.
Unlike a decorator, a proxy often creates or guards the real object itself.
In a chain, each handler either answers the request or passes it on.
Handlers know only the next link, so you reorder them without edits.

code.caption: Three requests, three different handlers answer. Build the chain as `Limit`, `Auth`, `Route` on lines 13–14 and watch `/b`.

walk.text: The base class stores the next handler; `setNext` returns it for chaining.
Default: pass the request on, or report that nobody took it.
`Auth` answers with 401 or calls `super.handle` to pass along.
`Limit` stops busy callers; otherwise it passes along.
`Route` ends the chain and always answers.
Build the chain once: `Auth`, then `Limit`, then `Route`.
Each request stops at the first handler that answers.

pitfalls: Keep the proxy's methods identical to the real object's, or callers break on swap.
End every chain with a default handler so no request disappears unanswered.
Order chain handlers on purpose: put cheap checks that reject many requests first.

quiz.why: The loop stops at the first handler that answers. The first handler already returns `negative` for -4, so the others never run.

takeaway: A proxy controls access to one object; a chain finds who handles a request.
